Notes for agents working on actimetrics.

agcounts and the “first second” padding

acti_calculate_counts() calls agcounts::calculate_counts(). When the data do not start on an epoch boundary (e.g. first sample at 18:41:00.5 for 60 s epochs), agcounts pads the start itself. Before agcounts PR #51 (issue #50) that padding was broken; fix_first_second_function() (R/ab_calculate_counts.R) pads the data before agcounts sees it, so the agcounts padding branch never runs (data_start == t1).

What agcounts PR #51 fixed (merged 2026-10-15, agcounts 0.7.1 on GitHub main)

  • Crash wrong sign in 'by' argument when the first sample was < 1 s after the epoch boundary (it padded with seq(data_start, t1 - 1, ...)).
  • A 1-second gap: padding stopped at t1 - 1 instead of just before t1.

With PR #51, counts are identical with and without our padding on the example GT3X (starts at 0.5 s and 37.5 s past the minute were checked).

What agcounts still gets wrong (as of PR #51)

  1. Extra columns: its padding is rbind(data.frame(time, X, Y, Z), raw), which errors (numbers of columns of arguments do not match) if raw has other columns (e.g. GENEActiv light, temperature). Only reachable with acti_calculate_counts(resample = FALSE): actibase::acti_resample() already drops non-XYZ columns.
  2. Spurious zero-count rows (agcounts issue #42): its expected-timestamp grid is built from the unaligned first time, so it appends zero rows that duplicate epochs (39 real minutes -> 78 rows). acti_calculate_counts() fixes this by flooring time to the epoch and summing.
  3. Version: Suggests requires agcounts (>= 0.6.7); the CRAN release may not contain PR #51.

Why we keep fix_first_second = TRUE as the default

Padding first avoids all three: agcounts sees aligned data, so neither its padding (rbind) nor its unaligned timestamp grid is used, regardless of the installed agcounts version. Our padding keeps all columns and attributes, uses an exact sample grid from the epoch start, and keeps the timezone.

acti_calculate_counts() also runs acti_standardize_data(subset_xyz = TRUE) first, so agcounts only ever sees time/X/Y/Z (this also maps names like TIME/HEADER_TIME_STAMP and lower-case x). That fixes (1) even with fix_first_second = FALSE, and keeps the sample_rate and transformations attributes. It does not fix (2) or (3), which is why the padding stays.

Do not remove the floor-and-sum step after agcounts::calculate_counts() or the padding without re-checking these cases.
